name: Ryan P. Seaman
summary: Biomedical informatics researcher and MMSc candidate at Harvard Medical School, seeking collaborative research and project roles in health technology and biotech.

bullets: Developing VitessceGen, a multi-agent AI tool that generates interactive visualization configurations from spatial and single-cell biomedical data.
Evaluating generated configurations against expert-authored examples using HuBMAP datasets, under Nils Gehlenborg's supervision.
Created the full annotation and narrative system within the existing Vitessce framework, with supervision and guidance from Mark S. Keller and Nils Gehlenborg.
Connected narrative text, saved views, and visual annotations into guided stories for spatial and single-cell data; manuscript in preparation.

experience.organization: MDI Biological Laboratory, Comparative Genomic and Data Science Core
bullets: Collaborated with research labs on biomedical data analysis and developed tools that help researchers explore their own datasets.
Built scscape, an open-source Nextflow pipeline for reproducible, multi-sample single-cell RNA sequencing analysis.
Maintained GCP/AWS infrastructure for research analysis and data storage.

education.detail: Waterville, ME | Varsity soccer, four years

skills.text: Python, R; biomedical data analysis and visualization; single-cell and spatial genomics.

publications.title: A cloud-based training module for efficient de novo transcriptome assembly using Nextflow and Google Cloud.

bullets: Co-taught a three-day single-cell course in 2024; created teaching materials and the course website.
Taught Python, held office hours, and mentored summer interns on computational research projects.
Coordinated the summer cohort's campus tours for prospective students and families.
